deck_subtitle: Cloud-aware learned pointing · making the problem engineerable

slides.title: Act I — Making the problem engineerable
bullets: Simulation, features, randomization, and a reproducible experiment pipeline

slides.title: Motivation: clouds waste imaging opportunities
bullets: Satellites have limited onboard storage and downlink capacity.
Cloud-blocked captures waste scarce imaging opportunities.
The valuable decision is not only where to image, but also when.

slides.title: Research question
bullets: Can a cloud-aware learned policy outperform the deterministic baseline on observation value?
Compare learned policies against a fixed sequential baseline under matched simulation conditions.
Focus on useful captures — not motion for its own sake.
Status after early experiments: hypothesis not yet supported on matched episode return.

slides.title: The bar: deterministic baseline (~393 mean return)
bullets: Baseline = SequentialTargetBaselinePolicy: fixed target list, best-estimate capture timing.
Matched warmup in SAC encoder run: return_mean ≈ 393, return_best ≈ 468 (summary_metrics.json).
This is the reference bar — not the smaller ~89 smoke-run warmup.
Every learned policy must be judged against this same-pipeline baseline.

slides.title: One system: sim → artifact → learn → render
bullets: One episode = one canonical simulation rollout (SimulationStateSeries).
Train, eval, and render consume the same simulation outputs.
Simulation owns physics, sensing, and reward; rendering is view-only.

slides.title: Features and reward — why learning could work
bullets: Observations: orbit, attitude, primary + secondary vision lines, shutter budget.
Actions: dim0 = control interface (see Act II); dim1 = shutter command.
Reward: image quality × coverage × novelty; penalties for budget waste and pointing effort.
Dense vision + shaped reward gives credit for timing clear windows — if the action interface is right.

slides.title: Randomization and experiment method
bullets: Episode = one polar overflight; pre-maneuver segment included in canonical rollout.

slides.title: Act II — Early experiments: hypothesis not proven
bullets: Learning signal yes; beating the ~393 baseline no — three action interfaces tested

slides.title: Returns vs the baseline bar
bullets: SAC compressed encoder (50 train eps): train return_mean ≈ 1.2, train_best ≈ 137, eval ≈ 81.
Warmup baseline in the same run: return_mean ≈ 393 — learned eval sits well below.
One high train episode is not beating the baseline; the mean curve does not cross the bar.
Dashed reference line in plot = deterministic warmup level.

slides.title: The learnability journey
bullets: Only runs with warmup baseline > 300 (fairly tuned deterministic reference).
Eval return (bars) vs same-run warmup (amber marker, ~393 for all shown).
Green = learning signal inferred; red = none. Best eval SAC encoder +81 — still below ~393 bar.
slides.notes: diagrams/results_scoreboard.png — data from summary_metrics.json per run

slides.title: MPO collapse (torque mode)
bullets: First MPO torque experiments: eval ≈ −243, torque saturation, shutter spam.
Safe-mode activations throughout — no useful captures.
Motivated systematic experiment pipeline and implementation fixes (dual-KL bug).

slides.title: Three ways to feed actions into the stack
bullets: Same shutter dim; dim0 semantics climb from low-level torque toward mission planning.
table: Built & run; learning_mode false — not successful yet

slides.title: Interface 1 vs 2: torque vs vector
bullets: Question: is torque too hard — should the agent command pointing, not wheel torque?
Both arms show a learning signal; neither approaches warmup ~393 on eval return.
SAC: torque eval −11.1 vs vector −24.1. MPO: vector +45.5 vs torque −81.1 — mode preference is algorithm-dependent.
Partial segregation helps diagnostics; does not close the mission gap yet.

slides.title: Interface 3: target selection + OBC (Exp 14)
bullets: Radical shift: Categorical(50) target + move + shutter; PD OBC when move=True.
Primary KPI = mission score (quality × coverage per capture), not raw return alone.
Multi-environment curriculum; eval on unseen env seeds.
Screen arm hp_default: learning_mode false; mission_score_mean ≈ 3.2; eval_return ≈ 0 — not successful yet.
Critical implementation bugs found and fixed before Phase 2; architecture reuse validated.

slides.title: What the experiments did prove
bullets: The problem is engineerable: reproducible runs, KPIs, videos, and isolated hypotheses.
Failures are diagnosable (MPO dual bug, encoder choice, reward penalties, action interface).
SAC and fixed MPO can learn non-trivial structure; MPO vector mode shows mode-dependent gains.
Superiority over the ~393 deterministic baseline on matched return: not demonstrated.

slides.title: Act III — Why we still believe this path
bullets: Segregate learning from low-level control; let AI choose what to point at

slides.title: Segregate concerns: planner · pilot · plant
bullets: North star: hierarchical mission planner over OBC low-level tracking.
Wrong split: RL learns raw torque — couples timing, dynamics, and safety arbitration.
Right split: RL chooses target / when to move / when to shoot; OBC closes the pointing loop.
Exp 14 is the first prototype of that split — early run unsuccessful, direction unchanged.

slides.title: Behavioral evidence below the return bar
bullets: Even when return < baseline, eval video shows structured pointing and shutter timing.
Behavioral claims require video — aggregate KPIs alone are insufficient.
Return gap may be reward shaping / interface / training budget — not absence of learning.
slides.notes: User-sign-off on frames before behavioral verdict in talk.

slides.title: Open work and close
bullets: Align training reward with mission score; iterate Exp 14 curriculum and factorized policy.
Matched eval protocol: same clouds / altitude / targets for best learned policy vs baseline ~393.
Continue climbing the action ladder: torque → vector → target select → full mission planner.
One-liner: we made cloud-aware onboard imaging an engineerable RL problem — hypothesis deferred, path convinced.
